correctness.rationale: For each fixed j>=3, a prescribed oriented edge adjacency in an independent random linear order has probability 1/n. The class weight w_{j,h} counts its 2^j compatible sign patterns, so E W_{j,h}=binom(n,2)binom(k,j)w_{j,h}/n^j exactly. For every fixed mixed factorial moment at k∼c n^{1-2/j}, same-underlying-edge repeated witnesses need at least j+1 distinct relation indices, costing k/n=O(n^{-2/j}); distinct edges with overlapping index subsets cost O(1/k); distinct edges with disjoint relation sets factor exactly, whether or not vertices overlap. Thus the independent Poisson limits with λ_{j,h}=w_{j,h}c^j/(2 j!) follow; convergence of masses plus tail truncation upgrades to TV. Markov below and retained-subfamily monotonicity above give sharp absence/presence; E Σ_e binom(M_e,j+1)=O(n^{-2/j}) rules out multiple witnesses per actual edge at criticality. The FO2 event is a different sentence for each growing vocabulary, not a fixed-language limit theorem. Direct enumeration of all n!^3 triples for n=2,3,4 independently confirms both h-class expectations.
residual_risks: Uniformly fixed j and independent uniform linear orders are essential; the proof is not uniform in growing j.
The exhaustive tests verify mean identities, not multivariate total-variation convergence.

originality.rationale: Bender–Canfield 1999 Theorem 1 yields a general Poisson law for the common edges in a fixed integer t of independently embedded sparse graphs. The key fixed-t common-edge rare mechanism is therefore prior art, but their theorem does not count all binom(k_n,j) combinations across growing k_n, nor resolve independent minority-direction strata at critical k_n∼n^{1-2/j}. Jeż–Michaliszyn–Witkowski 2026 establishes finite satisfiability of FO2 with many independent successors, not probabilities of random successor structures. The growing-label collision classification is assessed original at best knowledge, with possible wider Poisson-approximation coverage.
residual_risks: A published Poisson approximation for sparse occupancy hypergraphs with a growing number of layers might already imply the result after a translation.
A fixed-collection graph-intersection theorem is related and could supply some of the proof mechanism; no novelty claimed for that mechanism.
